name: Nebraska
permitAge: 15 (LPD learner’s permit), parent or guardian consent; 14 for the school learner’s permit (LPE) (secondary sources)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours logged and signed by a licensed driver at least 21, or an approved driver safety course (247 NAC 11-003); some secondary sources add 10 at night, not in the rule text
teen.holdPermit: 6 months on an LPE, SCP or LPD before the POP at 16 (secondary sources; one says 1 year)
teen.nightLimit: POP: no driving midnight to 6 a.m. unless to or from work or a school activity, or with a licensed driver 21 or older (Neb. Rev. Stat. 60-4,120.01)
teen.passengerLimit: POP, first 6 months: no more than one passenger under 19 who is not immediate family (Neb. Rev. Stat. 60-4,120.01)
teen.phone: POP: no interactive wireless device while driving (secondary enforcement). All drivers: texting banned, also while stopped in traffic (Neb. Rev. Stat. 60-6,179.01).

notes: LPD supervisor: licensed adult 21 or older in the front passenger seat (secondary sources; one adds two years of experience, unconfirmed).
Knowledge test 25 questions, 20 correct (80 percent): third-party practice sites only, all agree; not confirmed on dmv.nebraska.gov.
Full operator’s license: age 17 and 12 months on the POP (secondary).
Move over law expanded by LB 530, in effect Sept. 3, 2025: move to an adjacent lane for stopped vehicles or vulnerable road users, or slow down if unable (news reports).
School bus: on a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, only same-direction traffic must stop (UNK safety card; LB 500 text).
Rural interstates generally 75 mph; urban 55 to 60 (news and travel guides).
Adult seat belt law is secondary; driver, front-seat occupants and children 6 to under 18 must buckle (Nebraska DOT).
Spanish handbook and Spanish test availability not confirmed.
